Subject: Evidence request: geo-hold snapshots + TTL deletion proofs (SOC2)

Stephanie —

Thanks again for the quick sync this morning. As part of our SOC 2 readiness review we need a narrow set of artifacts that demonstrate Redwood's handling of snapshot retention and geo-hold behavior across regions. Can you confirm you can provide the following by end of next week (EOD 2026-01-29)?

Requested items (short list):
- Manifest of immutable snapshots (index showing snapshot id, creation_ts, region, retention_ttl) for the last 12 months
- Example proof of deletion for a tenant snapshot (trace/log + export hash)
- A copy of the retention policy that describes TTL semantics and geo-hold overrides
- Mapping showing where tenant data and snapshots are stored by AWS region for our account

If full exports are large, a sampled set with clear sampling methodology is fine — call out any redactions and why. Also confirm whether snapshot manifests are immutable (signed/hashes) or if they rely on internal audit logs.

We’ll route the artifacts to our audit team; let me know if you need a secure upload location or a time to walk through the artifacts.

Emily Barker

Thanks — a few implementation clarifications before we hand off finalized files to Emily: 

1) Sampling method: Stephanie, can you confirm the sampling seed (we should pick tenants across three size bands and two regions). I'll create the sample export script to ensure reproducibility and include the hash of the seed file in the manifest.

2) Deletion proof: our TTL deletion pipeline has two phases — mark expired (logical) and hard delete (physical). For SOC2 we should include both the mark event (audit-log entry with retention policy id) and the subsequent object-level deletion event (S3 delete marker + storage reclaim timestamp). The ttl-proof-sample.txt should therefore include both events with correlated request IDs.

3) Geo-hold overrides: confirm whether Northshore requested any geo-hold exceptions historically (Marissa — do we have any recorded exceptions for this account?). If yes, we need to include the exception ticket id and justification.

I’ll prepare the reproducible export and manifest signing instructions; sending a draft by EOD 21st for review.

Vivek Kulkarni
VP, Platform Reliability (SRE)
Redwood Inference

Emily — attaching the sampled artifacts and a short plan for the walkthrough. Thanks to the internal team for the quick turnaround.

Included items (attachments + links):
- snapshot-index-2025Q4.csv (sampled manifest, 120 entries, includes ETag & manifest checksum)
- ttl-proof-sample.txt (logical mark + object delete events with request IDs and audit-log refs)
- retention-policy-v3.pdf (policy with geo-hold override highlighted)
- region-mapping.csv (tenant sample mapping; full mapping available under NDA)

What we did:
- Sampling: tenants selected using a reproducible seed (sha256: a3f4c2e...), stratified by tenant size (small/medium/large) and region (us-east-1, eu-west-1). The seed file hash is included as the first line in snapshot-index-2025Q4.csv.
- Immutable manifests: manifests are written to a dedicated S3 bucket with server-side checksum and versioning enabled; we included the manifest S3 path + object ETag for each entry. We also generated a detached signature (DocuSign link below) for the sampled manifest set.
- Deletion proof: ttl-proof-sample.txt shows correlated audit-log entries (audit_id) for the mark and for the physical delete; we include object-level ETags pre-delete and post-delete tombstone markers.

Delivery mechanism: secure Drive folder (link below). If you prefer SFTP, tell us and we’ll push the full export.

Proposed walkthrough: 30 minutes on Tue 01/27 10:00 PT — I’ll demo manifest structure, sampling reproducibility, and trace linking between TTL mark and hard-delete events. Confirm time or propose alternate.

Links / Uploads: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aBcd-NS-SOC2-Northshore (uploaded)
Detached signature envelope: DocuSign://envelope/0fa1b2c3d4e5f6

If you want an attestation letter (signed by Redwood legal) we can prepare that as a separate deliverable; Marissa will coordinate with procurement for contract-level artifacts.

Best —
